proposed_fix.description: Confirm the cartservice socket anomaly and its error source, then, only if approved, restart or scale cartservice to clear exhausted or stuck connections.
steps: Inspect cartservice socket state per pod (e.g. ss -s / netstat counts of ESTABLISHED, TIME_WAIT, CLOSE_WAIT) and compare with baseline to see if the cartservice_socket rise in E1 is leaked or stuck connections.
Pull the full text of the gRPC 'Error status code' lines in E4 to identify the actual status (the text is truncated) and which callers or downstream dependency (e.g. Redis) are failing.
Check whether the trace error rate in E2 (0.12) lines up in time with the frontend error spike in E1, to confirm cartservice is the source and not just a victim.
If CLOSE_WAIT/connection counts are abnormally high on specific pods, and after human approval, do a rolling restart of cartservice one pod at a time, watching error rate between pods.
If load-related, and after approval, add one replica of cartservice temporarily and observe the socket and error metrics.
preconditions: Confirm with the on-call engineer that cartservice has at least 2 healthy replicas so a rolling restart does not cause a full outage.
Verify the E4 error status code and that the errors are not caused by a failing downstream dependency, which a restart would not fix.
Capture current socket counts, error rate and pod state for comparison before any change.
proposed_fix.rollback: Restart is not reversible per se, but it is done one pod at a time and halted if errors rise; remove the added replica by scaling back to the original replica count, and restore the original deployment spec if any config was changed.
